core_obligations: Compare D with the algebraic dualizing functor on affines to see that it preserves coherent objects (proof lines 489-508).

difficulty_reason: For a dualizing complex K on a locally Noetherian scheme X, the lemma asserts that K lies in D_Coh(O_X) and that D = RSheafHom(-, K) induces an anti-equivalence of D_Coh(O_X) with itself equipped with a canonical isomorphism id -> D o D; if X is quasi-compact then D exchanges D^+_Coh and D^-_Coh and induces an anti-equivalence of D^b_Coh (statement lines 471-487). The proof takes an affine open U = Spec(A), lets omega_A^bullet be the dualizing complex for A corresponding to K|_U by Lemma labelled lemma-equivalent-definitions, and uses Lemma labelled lemma-affine-duality to see that the diagram comparing RSheafHom(-, K|_U) with RHom_A(-, omega_A^bullet) commutes, so D preserves D_Coh(O_X) (proof lines 489-508). Then the canonical map L -> RSheafHom(K, K) otimes^L L -> RSheafHom(RSheafHom(L, K), K), whose second arrow is the evaluation map of Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-internal-hom-evaluate, is an isomorphism for all L because this holds on affines by Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-dualizing; the footnote records the alternative route of first showing RSheafHom(K, K) = O_X and then using Lemma labelled lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isom part (2). The statement about boundedness for quasi-compact X also follows from the algebraic lemma (proof lines 510-526). Comparing the functor with its affine model and transferring the algebraic inverse equivalence to the scheme level is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
